name: Zinder and the Sultan's Palace
subtitle: Zinder, in southern Niger, was the capital of the Damagaram sultanate from 1736.

facts.label: Capital moved to Zinder
facts.value: The sultan of Damagaram moved the capital to Zinder in 1736

facts.label: Role
facts.value: Zinder began as a small Hausa village and became a hub of trans-Saharan trade

facts.label: Palace construction
facts.value: Said to have been built under Sultan Tanimoune between 1850 and 1852

facts.label: Seat at Birni
facts.value: Sultan Souleymane Dan Tanimoune installed the sultanate's seat in Birni, Zinder

facts.label: Sultans
facts.value: 26 sultans ruled for 200 years until the early 20th century

facts.label: French conquest
facts.value: A French column attacked Zinder on 13 September 1899, killing Sultan Amadou Kouran Daga

facts.label: Today
facts.value: The sultanate continues as a largely ceremonial position and the sultan lives in the palace

facts.label: Ownership
facts.value: The palace belongs to the sultanate

parts.text: Zinder, in southern Niger, was the capital of the Damagaram sultanate from 1736. The sultan's palace in the Birni quarter is said to date from 1850-1852. The sultanate was ended by a French attack in 1899, but the line of sultans continues as a largely ceremonial office.

gaps: The description is summarised from the sources listed here and should be read against them.
